text:
Alice: Heads up - customer-facing batch job started hitting AccessDenied on KMS Decrypt after role swap. Error from service: "User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/BatchProcessorRole/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef12-3456 because the key policy or grants deny it"
Ben: Can you paste the full CloudTrail event or the KMS error payload? and the key ARN?
Alice: Key ARN is arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef12-3456. CloudTrail shows DecodeFailure with "AccessDenied" and the event has no EncryptionContext on the Decrypt call. Here's the event snippet:
```
{
  "eventName": "Decrypt",
  "userIdentity": {"arn": "arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/BatchProcessorRole/session", "accountId": "222222222222"},
  "errorMessage": "AccessDenied",
  "requestParameters": {"ciphertextBlob": "...", "encryptionContext": null}
}
```
Carla: Interesting — the key policy for that KMS key has a conditional that requires either (a) caller is account 222222222222 OR (b) the principal has tag `team:infra` on the session. Policy excerpt:
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowAccountOrTaggedPrincipals",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "*"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalAccount": "222222222222"},
    "ForAnyValue:StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/team": "infra"}
  }
}
```
Carla: That policy is unusual (mixing account check + principal tags). If the role is assumed via STS, tags on the source principal aren't automatically present on the assumed session unless `Tags` were passed when calling AssumeRole and `TransitiveTagKeys` are configured on the role.
Josh: Confirmed - the role assumption path is cross-account (account 333333333333 -> assume role in 222222222222). The assume-role call wasn't passing session tags. We rely on session tags in prod for RBAC but they aren't being propagated here.
Maya: Two quick checks: 1) Is there an IAM grant on the KMS key that explicitly allows the assumed-role ARN? 2) Are there any active KMS grants (GrantTokens) that might let this caller decrypt?
Ben: Checked grants: no explicit grant for the assumed-role. There are grants for a service principal (kms:ViaService for lambda.amazonaws.com) but not for our batch role. Grants are usually used by services, not by cross-account assumed roles in our setup.
Alice: So root cause theory: conditional key policy requires a principal tag that isn't present on the STS session, so KMS denies. But why didn't IAM policy allow it? The role's IAM policy includes kms:Decrypt on that key ARN. Yet KMS evaluates the key policy and conditions take precedence; if key policy denies, request fails.
Carla: Exactly. KMS enforces the key policy first. If the key policy condition evaluates false, neither IAM policy nor grants will help unless a grant explicitly allows the principal OR the key policy is changed.
Josh: Quick repro: I ran `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/BatchProcessorRole --role-session-name test` and then attempted decrypt with that session creds -> AccessDenied. When I re-ran assume-role with `--tags team=infra --transitive-tag-keys team` and retried, Decrypt succeeded.
Alice: Good find. So we have two remediation options: (A) change the key policy to accept the assumed-role (explicit ARN principal) OR relax the conditional to check aws:PrincipalAccount only OR (B) update the role usage to pass session tags and ensure callers include the tag. Which is safer?
Maya: For immediate mitigation we can add an explicit Principal entry for the BatchProcessorRole ARN in the key policy (short-lived change) and follow up with a longer-term design (session tags). Also add audit entries so we know who assumed roles without tags.
Ben: Note: adding the role ARN to the key policy will grant that role permanently unless we add a time-bound mechanism (not native in key policy). Consider creating a KMS grant that authorizes the assumed-role and set Retiring principals and an expiry via automation (rotate/remove). Grants can be retired but are less visible in the key policy.
Carla: Also double-check encryption context usage in the app. If Decrypts are expected to require a specific EncryptionContext, missing context will also cause AccessDenied. But CloudTrail showed encryptionContext null here. If the producer included a context at Encrypt time, Decrypt must present same context.
Alice: App code uses envelope encryption via our client helper; it should pass context but when role swap occurred we saw null — possibly stripped by intermediate service. We'll triage that path.
Josh: For audit: CloudTrail shows Decrypt AccessDenied with "principalSessionTags": [] for these events. I'll open a ticket for tagging enforcement gaps and link to the bucket of failing jobs.
SecBot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-decrypt-accessdenied — follow checklist: 1) check key policy conditions 2) check grants 3) check encryption context 4) confirm STS tags/transitive keys 5) rotate/create temporary grant for urgent unblocking.
Maya: I'll prepare a minimal-policy PR to add "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/BatchProcessorRole" to the key policy on a temp basis. Josh can test, then we remove after session-tagged flow is in place.
Alice: Sounds good. Also please record the CloudTrail event IDs for compliance. I'll assign the follow-up to SecOps.
Ben: One more gotcha: If any KMS Grant was created by AWS on behalf of a service, it may include an EncryptionContext restriction — watch out when creating new grants.
Carla: TL;DR: AccessDenied caused by conditional key policy expecting principal tags that weren't present on STS session; workaround = explicit principal or temporary grant; long-term = ensure callers pass session tags or change key policy to rely on account-based checks.
Alice: Thanks all — will update the incident tracker with the chosen path.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread about KMS Decrypt AccessDenied caused by conditional key policy and missing STS session tags
